title: The task
body: Sort **[5, 2, 4, 1]** with insertion sort. The left part of the array is the sorted part. Each round takes the next item, `j`, and swaps it left while its left neighbor is bigger, like sliding a new card into a sorted hand.

title: Place 2
body: `j` points at 2. Its left neighbor 5 is bigger, so they swap. Now 2 is at the front and nothing is left of it: this round is done.

title: Place 4
body: `j` points at 4. Its neighbor 5 is bigger, so they swap. Next to 4 is now 2, which is smaller, so 4 stops. The sorted part is [2, 4, 5].

predict.question: 4 swaps past 5. Does it also swap past 2?
options: Yes, 4 always goes to the front
No, 2 is smaller than 4, so 4 stops
predict.explanation: Insertion sort stops as soon as the left neighbor is not bigger. 2 < 4, so 4 stays at index 1.

title: Place 1: first swap
body: The last item, 1, is smaller than everything in the sorted part, so it has the longest trip. First it swaps with 5.

title: Place 1: second swap
body: 4 is bigger than 1, so they swap.

title: Place 1: third swap
body: 2 is bigger than 1, so they swap. 1 reaches index 0, where nothing is left of it, and the round ends.

predict.question: How many swaps did the whole sort make?
predict.explanation: 1 swap for 2, 1 for 4, and 3 for 1: 5 in total. Each swap fixes one pair that was out of order, and [5, 2, 4, 1] had 5 such pairs.

title: Done
body: The array is sorted: **[1, 2, 4, 5]**. In the worst case (reverse order) every item swaps past all the items before it: 0 + 1 + 2 + … + (n − 1) = n(n − 1)/2 swaps, which is O(n²). On an already sorted array no item moves: O(n).
